findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion in Session Value Access (codeVerifier)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion causes panic if session value is missing or wrong type
findings.evidence: Line 82: `oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_verifier", session.Values["codeVerifier"].(string))` performs unsafe type assertion without checking if codeVerifier exists or is a string
findings.recommendation: Use safe type assertion with ok check: `if cv, ok := session.Values["codeVerifier"].(string); ok { ... } else { /* handle error */ }`

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion in Session Value Access (codeChallenge)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion
findings.evidence: Line 82: `oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_challenge", session.Values["codeChallenge"].(string))` without checking if value exists or is correct type
findings.recommendation: Validate session values with ok check before type assertion

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion in Session Value Access (requestedURL)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion on requestedURL
findings.evidence: Line 111: `requestedURL := session.Values["requestedURL"].(string)` performs type assertion without validation
findings.recommendation: Check value existence and type: `if rv, ok := session.Values["requestedURL"].(string); ok { requestedURL = rv }`

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion in Session Value Access (failcount)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion on failcount value
findings.evidence: Line 80: `failcount = session.Values[requestedURL].(int)` without checking if value exists or is int type
findings.recommendation: Use safe type assertion: `if fc, ok := session.Values[requestedURL].(int); ok { failcount = fc }`

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion in Session Value Access (state)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion on state value
findings.evidence: Line 251: `var state string = session.Values["state"].(string)` without validation
findings.recommendation: Validate session state with type checking

findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion
findings.evidence: Line 279: `oauth2.SetAuthURLParam("code_challenge", session.Values["codeChallenge"].(string))` without checking if value exists or is string

findings.title: Critical Bug in JWT Token Decompression - Read After Close on Gzip Reader
findings.impact: Token decompression fails silently - gzip reader is closed before reading, causing empty token parsing or read-after-close error
findings.evidence: Line 202: `if err := zr.Close(); err != nil` closes the gzip reader BEFORE line 205 `ss, _ := io.ReadAll(zr)` tries to read from it. The order is wrong - reader is closed before it's read.
findings.recommendation: Reverse the order: read from gzip reader first, THEN close it. Change to: `ss, _ := io.ReadAll(zr); if err := zr.Close(); err != nil { ... }`

findings.title: Potential Out-of-Bounds Access in Multipart Cookie Reassembly
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - malformed cookie parts can cause array index out of bounds
findings.evidence: Line 136: `cookieParts[i-1] = cookie.Value` assigns to array without bounds checking. If cookie name is '3of2', the index would be 2 but array size is only 2 (indices 0-1)
findings.recommendation: Add bounds validation: `if i > 0 && i <= numParts { cookieParts[i-1] = cookie.Value } else { return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid cookie part index") }`

findings.title: HTTP Header Injection via Custom Claims
findings.impact: HTTP Response Splitting / Header Injection - custom claims are added directly to HTTP headers without sanitization
findings.evidence: Line 104: `w.Header().Add(header, strings.Join(strs, ","))` adds arbitrary JWT claims to HTTP headers. Newlines in claims could inject headers.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize header values by rejecting claims containing CR/LF characters or validate that Go's http.Header rejects injection attempts

findings.title: Sensitive Tokens Exposed in Debug Logs
findings.impact: Information Disclosure - response headers including auth tokens logged at debug level
findings.evidence: Line 75-76: `fastlog.Debug("response header", zap.Any("all headers", w.Header()))` logs all headers which may contain access tokens and ID tokens (set at lines 67, 70)
findings.recommendation: Avoid logging auth tokens. Filter sensitive headers before logging.

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion for OAuth Token Extra Claims
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion on OAuth token extra claims
findings.evidence: Line 44: `ptokens.PIdToken = providerToken.Extra("id_token").(string)` performs unsafe type assertion without checking if Extra returns a string
findings.recommendation: Use safe type assertion: `if idToken, ok := providerToken.Extra("id_token").(string); ok { ptokens.PIdToken = idToken }`

findings.title: Unsafe Type Assertion for OAuth Token Extra Claims (HomeAssistant)
findings.impact: Denial of Service (panic) - unchecked type assertion
findings.evidence: Line 39: `ptokens.PAccessToken = providerToken.Extra("access_token").(string)` without checking if value is string type

findings.title: Ignored Error from JSON Unmarshal
findings.impact: Silent failure - if JSON parsing fails, malformed data may be used for authentication
findings.evidence: Line 106: `json.Unmarshal([]byte(idToken), &adfsUser)` error is not checked. If parsing fails, adfsUser will be zero-valued and authentication may proceed incorrectly
findings.recommendation: Check error: `if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(idToken), &adfsUser); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf(...) }`
